notes.title: Weekly Update 82 - FPS and Ghosts
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/89294fd71553f68f16c33e42b2d322818dd28471.png[/img][h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
As mentioned last week, I will briefly explain some of the optimisation I’ve been doing over the last few weeks, and show some of the bugs that have occurred as a result!

As I already explained a little while ago, our primary goal in setting up the island had been to first make it look good - and to optimise after. When the island was finished, this meant that there were some areas in which my FPS (on ultra) dropped as low as 15, which was obviously not good enough. As a result, I decided to focus on optimisation for a little bit. 

I have had a long list of possible ways to optimise the game for months now, but considering that it hadn’t been needed yet, I had largely ignored that list (and I am still ignoring much of it). However, one of our large bottlenecks was the rendering done on the CPU side, and so I used a number of measures to try to move as much of that rendering over to the GPU as possible.

The result is now a decent 30 FPS in the most demanding areas of the map, and up to 60 FPS in less demanding areas. While this could still be improved, I have moved on to optimising the combat between pirates and soldiers for now, considering there is another bottleneck there, and 30 FPS is sufficient for the time being. 

However, with the optimisation came a range of new visual bugs, some of which we found particularly amusing: 

For one, many of the trees hadn’t been set up properly, and they ended up never disappearing when they got cut down (see above). Our sawmills then ended up cutting down whole forests that were just lying around, which led to a lush if somewhat wasteful look of the forests afterwards.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/54bab29751c7f6a71f7aaac6ed7faf1493a96140.jpg[/img]

For another, when playing in co-op, the allied commander turned into somewhat of a genie/ghost (see today’s picture). I still haven’t figured out what exactly was happening here, but from a certain range on, the other commander simply disappeared from the bottom up. 

I will keep working on the optimisation and bug fixing, and will keep you updated!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 81 - Art Direction
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e616eeb0f86d9781f3293561e7c6ea6f3fb27264.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week was fairly productive, and while I initially planned on discussing some of the optimisation (I managed to get a minimum of 30 FPS in my latest build) and the bugs ensuing from it, I think this blog may be better spent on explaining why everything is taking longer than expected.

When we started this project, John was taking care of the entire art side of the project. This came with a steep learning curve, many failed (and successful) attempts, and ultimately resulted in what I believe to be a relatively unique artstyle for the game, which John and I both enjoy. 

For a number of professional and personal reasons, John has not been able to dedicate as much time to the project as of last year as we both would have liked, and as a result, I took over a lot of the art side responsibilities, such as creating shaders as well as the world building for Pirates’ Peak. While a lot of the code for 0.8 had already been finished by mid last year, this meant that creating the art for 0.8 now had to happen after, and it has as a result taken a lot longer than expected.

At this point, we decided that we should try to bring in additional artists that could help us bridge some of the gap between the time John can work on the game and the speed at which we would like to progress. This did, however, come with additional issues: a lot of the artstyle of the game developed very organically, lots of it (e.g. the buildings and villagers) are still mostly placeholders, and we now had to communicate to other artists what we needed from them. Today’s image shows two buildings for comparison: the smelter (right) being an early placeholder building, while the charcoal hut (left) is a more recent building, much closer to what we want (but not finalised yet).

As a result, a lot of John’s and my recent work has been dedicated to trying to determine how to put our process on creating art into clear instructions for others, to plan for future art direction and developments, and to try to figure out exactly where we wanted to draw the line for further improvements. I am glad to say that I think we have finally gotten a good idea of that, even though we still have to work out some of the details.

Knowing the direction we want to take has also meant that we could focus on creating some high quality assets that would be shared among the buildings, and that could help us create a consistent feel. In that sense, John has recently been focusing on creating new materials for the various walls, roofs, etc. of the buildings, and we really like the approach and outcome we have ended up with. It will be a little while before we have enough of these assets to create the new buildings, but putting them together from well made assets should really speed up our process.

With that being said, we also decided that we would create some of the new buildings as placeholders again, so we can turn them out quickly, and finally get to experimental branch 0.8 even before finalising all of the high quality assets.

More on the optimisation and bugs next week!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 80 - The Rich Lake Biome
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/22ab93e37ef67e7f22266b69c1f5207e41ccf28e.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
I was travelling last week, so haven’t been able to do as much optimisation as I had hoped - but we finally finished upgrading the last assets for the last biome: the Rich Lake. So without further ado, let me introduce this new area!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/ae738f63c62c2852dcf2da49caeac6d7079258da.png[/img]

The Rich Lake area comes directly after the Iron Plateau - and when players have access to the final tier of buildings and soldiers. The biome is dominated by tropical pine trees and a big lake in the middle, with very little vegetation below the canopy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/f18f2f8e07955dc165ea12c0b8c28f01c7d933ce.png[/img]

The result is a very open area, which does not hide a great deal of loot, while being host to a vast amount of pirates, as well as a large amount of possible mineral vein spawns, which give the area its name.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/3bb601a08c31a570eba74a2ec363dbf732522a6f.png[/img]

The Rich Lake area is largely designed to be a final push for the players - after receiving access to all technology, fighting their way through the Rich Lake will get them face to face with the final Pirate Fortress, which will hold the artefact that needs to be retrieved to win. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/7f38e4cfdb757517202bfd83af9da96a3ce33f86.png[/img]

This means that it will be necessary for players to fight their way through the Rich Lake against increasingly large groups of pirate attack waves (assuming they are switched on), and every metre ground gained will be hard fought over. Any ground you do gain, however, will be rewarded with extra mines that may allow you to bolster your forces or establish a final fortress of your own from which to stage your attack.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 79 - A New Sound System
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/b3c061ddfed3f008b83696fcca494b058e36fb17.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
There were many smaller improvements and developments that happened last week, many of which were not particularly flashy, so I will be talking about one of the bigger ones that happened over the past few weeks instead: switching the system through which we deal with sounds!

Many of you who are playing the currently available version know that we had not included too many sounds yet by the time we uploaded this version. Over the past couple of months, we created a lot of new sounds for nature, buildings, and villagers - and I had managed to at least introduce a few of them into the development build already.

However, we quickly realised two limitations: firstly, adding many sounds to the default Unity audio system came with a lot of bugs and problems, and so a lot of the time spent adding sounds turned into figuring out why the sound wasn’t behaving the way it should. Secondly, and adding to that, we have a long, long list of things that I need to be doing on the game, especially as I had to take on a decent amount of art and world building tasks, which meant that finding time to add sounds (and figuring out their bugs) was becoming increasingly difficult. 

As a result, Haakon offered to be working on the sounds directly in Unity. For this, we also wanted to change to a different underlying sound system which Haakon was more familiar with and which was going to give us more options, and we have been working on migrating to this new sound system and getting Haakon set up on the project for a little while now. Of course, this migration came with many problems itself, not all of which are fixed yet, but hopefully this initial pain will be worth it when we can add more sounds much quicker in the future. 

I will keep you posted on the progress.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 78 - Optimising the Island
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/3fe52e676bec4cbe2e5c3d3c0326f80be59780c1.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
As we are waiting for art assets to come along, I’ve done a decent amount of bug fixing, QoL improvements, and optimisation in the past week - the bigger ones of which I will try to explain today:

First of all, I was finally able to fix the game’s behaviour when a coop partner left the game. So far, when a coop partner left the game, the game would essentially hand control of all the buildings to the remaining player (including the other commander), which led to all sorts of issues, including the menu not working properly after. This was difficult to solve for a variety of reasons, which largely come down to me having set the game up for PvP initially, with the strong possibility of capturing an opponent’s buildings. Since switching to a PvE and coop focus, I could restructure how the game was set up, which now allows us to delete a leaving player’s assets more easily. 

Secondly, I was finally able to fully address a concern that many people have had: widescreen support. While I had tried to fix some UI issues for widescreen monitors before, it wasn’t until last week that I was once again reminded of the issue, and decided to look into fixing it. I am pleased to say that widescreens should now be fully supported for 0.8 as soon as it is on the experimental branch.

Beyond some smaller fixes, such as correcting how ground shrubbery got removed, I was also able to address some of the performance issues we’ve had: While my first priority over the past few months had been to set the world up as well as we could, this has also meant that performance had suffered in some areas. In fact, some parts of the island ended up dropping my FPS as low as 15 - which is obviously not acceptable, despite only happening on ultra quality. Over the past 2 weeks, I was able to identify a couple of bottlenecks that led to these issues, and I’ve already been able to improve the lows from 15 to 25 FPS. The bottlenecks are by no means removed yet, but I will keep at it, and I am quite encouraged by the fact that there are very distinct bottlenecks that lend themselves to fixing, rather than just consistently bad or mediocre performance across all areas which would be much more difficult to address.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 77 - The Iron Plateau
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e32d877e367af07586d233f3aa30001f256b00ec.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week was pretty productive again, with me finally having some time to look at performance optimisation of the new island - but more on that next week, this week I promised to introduce the next biome: the Iron Plateau.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/a5095ec6cdf53bb0c4a89f6123d5f22a3314a092.png[/img]

The Iron Plateau follows immediately after the Jungle, and as you can see from the pictures, has a very different vibe. It is a very open area reminiscent of the Grasslands, but unlike the Grasslands, is full of pirates. In addition to many random groupings of pirates protecting the various loot across the biome, two of the pirate fortresses are in the area as well, which means that you will have your hands full if you want to secure it for yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/b18bdd8804b08d26ee9fe375509eb7b7e0c2a759.png[/img]

In good news, however, the Iron Plateau will be the first area that gives you access to, you guessed it, iron mines. With lots of space to expand to and fertile enough ground for farming, this should allow you to create a sizable outpost for mining, and it will give you access to the third tier of buildings and units. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/b18bdd8804b08d26ee9fe375509eb7b7e0c2a759.png[/img]

With only one more biome left between this area and the final pirate fortress (and the artefact it holds), your base in the Iron Plateau will also be a perfect staging area for your final push into the island, so securing it against the pirates should be a big priority.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 76 - The Jungle Biome
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/c7bf44c2e72714e0988aa68e033d2a45ec19737b.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week was very productive; we finalised the assets for the Jungle (and therefore also the biome itself), fixed a range of bugs, and are getting ever closer to uploading 0.8. As usual, I will show you the Jungle biome today!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/de276901cd1b52d28d5b256995c1182c9ac282f9.png[/img]

The Jungle is the biome you will get into after the Stone Valleys. Unlike the Stone Valleys, however, the Jungle is a lush environment with lots of water, trees, and shrubbery. This makes it a surprisingly dangerous environment to move through - considering pirates can lurk behind every corner, and you may come face to face with pirate pistoleers without much notice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/caa02f67957d21fd78b4640a09f63e89c69e99c6.png[/img]

In terms of resources, the Jungle will provide you with lots of wood - and a decent amount of expansion space once you cut down some trees. The Jungle will also be the first area in which you will be able to find coal mines - which will give you a much better option to get coal than burning copious amounts of wood. As a result, the Jungle will be a necessary step toward sustainable ammo production. The Jungle is also host to a number of banana trees, so it should provide your villagers with some food right off the bat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e19fea71c97dea4e93edc887106132e492ae030c.png[/img]

Finally, the lush environment has given us many, many options to hide paths into the mountains and loot, so once you decide to brave the danger of running into pirates at every corner, you will also be able to get a reward around most corners!

The next biome, the Iron Plateau, has been ready for a few weeks now, so I will show you a sneak peak of it next week.

Until next week!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/db6dfd28c3d2a728c3ab5f4b1ace27a4c6ed728c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/71a52df9cfbb65cd4bb22cb4266cab8313e7d431.png[/img]
(The coal ore without the mine seen in today's main image)

The first big difference between the new mines and the ones we had previously is the adaptive material. Considering our mountain rocks adapt to the humidity of their environment to show different levels of weathering and moss growth, we needed to bring the mineral veins in line to have them stand out less (so you and your scouts actually need to go looking for them). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/09aaab4004858a3cff7ba792ddba7f390d3bb342.png[/img]

(Gold ore and mine in the jungle area - consider this a sneak peak!)

Adjusting the material, however, meant that the way in which mineral veins and mines could previously be recognised (by lines drawn on them by hand) had to be changed. As a result, we decided to add physical objects of each mineral to the ore rocks and mines, which will also adapt depending on whether a mine is placed at the location or not.

The result is an ore rock that will fit in with the mountain rocks wherever it is placed, and that has a much nicer representation of the ore it actually has. Overall, I am quite pleased with the outcome!

I had said that we would aim to release 0.8 to experimental by now, but given that we needed to also create some new art assets for the jungle, this has to be pushed a little more. Uploading to experimental is now mostly waiting for those assets to finish and for our final buildings to be updated, so we are mostly ready – but I really want the experimental build to at least have a consistent looking world, so this needs to be included.

Once 0.8 is released on experimental, I am planning to update the tutorial, work on sounds, and ideally add 3 more units to the game before the proper launch. On John’s end, we are hoping to get the new villagers into the game at that stage, and to polish their animations as much as possible.

Apart from a minor bug fix, our last update available to players was uploaded in April last year. That is clearly too long. We stopped updating frequently at that point to be able to release all the features of the new update together, but with all of the changes that occur in the development of a game like ours, there are too many unforeseen delays to bundle an update like that. As a result, we will be introducing the experimental branch with the first upload of 0.8 soon, and while we may take our time to upload an update to the main branch again, we will continuously update the experimental branch to reflect the current state of the game’s development – do no more long waits like this.

With that, we also hope to be getting more timely feedback from a larger group of players, which should ultimately help us to make this the best game it can be!

notes.title: Weekly Update 72 - Pirate Fortresses
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/c66e909c53d288fff14fe41c76c35aff9a5a7e9d.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week saw a decent amount of bug fixing and world building, but we are still missing some assets to finalise the jungle and the lake plateau, so you’ll need to wait a little longer to see pictures of them. In the meantime, I want to talk a little about the pirate fortresses that will be one of the bigger focuses of the new map.

Before now, there were a range of pirate camps distributed around the island(s), which served as both small groups of pirates that would protect an area, as well as being the spawn points for pirate waves. Some of the camps were placed strategically to defend certain areas or things (for example the artefact that needs to be collected to win), while others were spawned randomly. Between both types, we hoped the place the pirate waves spawned would be sufficiently random that players would need to defend from all sides, and that progression would be slowed down by them.

With us doubling down on PvE and a stronger focus on progression, we decided to upgrade the pirate camps and their role. Instead of just placing multiple camps next to each other to increase the amount of pirates and having potentially dozens of spawn points across the world, we decided to create much more interesting, hand-crafted fortresses that will be waiting for you in strategically placed locations across the island, and will present challenges according to your current level of progression. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/ed9f99d0fd10530febec319a9970d512cfb67716.png[/img]
The first fortress will be found in the stone valleys. You can expand into the stone valleys in a way that allows you to circumvent the fortress, but that means you will continuously have to deal with pirate waves spawning behind you if you don't take care of it. The fortress is down a little inclined, which means that you have a advantage when assaulting it, but there is a formidable force in the fortress, so don't take the assault lightly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e25d37a9ab709141096caf73831cc1a2f4b9f11b.png[/img]
The second (above) and third fortress (main image today) will be found around the metal plateaus, blocking your advancement and providing further possibilities to get attacked from behind if you don't take care of them.

The last fortress will be at the end of the island and will contain the artefact. This one will be the most heavily fortified of them, so prepare carefully before you attack it! I will not include a picture of it here so you will have to scout to find it for yourself.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 68 - The Stone Valleys Biome
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/1731b56bb3a2afd8ebe7ff07085348e1988d36ef.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
I was able to make very good progress this week, including introducing some new loot, creating the first pirate fortress (more on that in another post), and I will take today to show you the next biome: The Stone Valleys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/4bb7bc47e6ed6c702ce8edaa9c852cd39b7ee60b.png[/img]
The first thing you will notice is that the Stone Valleys are a lot drier than the previous two biomes. Once the humidity map doesn’t just affect mountains, but also whether you can place fields (and what type of fields), this will become an area in which it won’t be possible to farm and sustain yourself with food, so you will need to send a generous amount of it from your main base. The biome also doesn’t have a lot of trees, which will make construction more difficult, and there is a decent amount of rocks coming up through the ground which will make building around them a bit of a challenge. Nevertheless, the biome is too far from your main base(s) to reach easily, so building an outpost here will be necessary to advance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/9157678dd09e9cd087ff02657b3f207d55a37792.png[/img]
To make up for all of this, however, the biome will be the first one to provide stone as a resource. With this stone, you will gain access to the next tier of construction, which will include access to gunpowder production, pistoleers, bread production, and a range of other things that will help you defend yourself (and advance further into the island).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/77f61f46f5d9070a4ebc899debb99b594571a537.png[/img]
As with the previous two biomes, there are many hidden paths and areas in which you can find loot and treasures (I have also introduced some of the new loot, such as buried treasures, baskets, etc), and you should have many chances to replenish your ammo here even before being able to create it yourself. 

Finally, the Stone Valleys also contain the first of the pirate fortresses, so you will have to raise a pretty sizable army to secure your expansion and to get whatever loot it contains. I will write a little more on the fortresses in the coming weeks to keep you up to date with how they will be interacting with the rest of the game.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 67 - Happy New Year
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/99754b78c718b0d4db3baf474c944772f29d91d5.png[/img]
[h1]Happy new year everyone![/h1]
First of all, let me apologise for the late blog - I had to travel and wasn’t able to connect my laptop to the internet for the past week. 

As you will undoubtedly have noticed by now, we also haven’t uploaded 0.8 to the experimental branch yet - John and I both had a lot of unforeseen work and personal responsibilities coming up over the last three weeks, so we have not been able to devote as much time to developing the game as we had hoped. I am supposed to be on holiday this week, so I will use as much of that time as possible on the game, and John will also be back to a more regular schedule. As a result, we are aiming to upload 0.8 onto the experimental branch in approximately three weeks, and we will try to get as close to the planned February date for the full 0.8 release as possible.

Moving on from scheduling, I’ll explain a recent idea we had when planning out how your villages may shape themselves in 0.9 as you progress through the game. We discussed the ground cover system a few blogs back and that system can also be utilised to add some man made ornaments in addition to plants.

The ground cover is coded so that it is removed when you place building blueprints that overlap with the cover - this will help avoid issues where plants clip through the buildings or cause graphical issues of grasses growing through floors. This does also mean, however, that we can add additional ground cover throughout the village during the game without these items stopping you from building your village however you like. For instance, when there is a build up of houses / buildings we can spawn in some lived in touches between the structures: Barrels and piles of bricks; Hay stacks or crates or tools (a mock-up of this is shown in today’s image). Different objects will add to the feel of the village, ensure that no two streets feel the same, and create the feeling of having neighbourhoods rather than just disjointed buildings. We can add extra items to be considered by this system and build up the variety that players experience over time.

Combined with the previously mentioned variety and randomness of certain parts of the buildings themselves, we are anticipating that this will add to the organic growth of the villages, making them feel more unique. This could become especially interesting to see if it makes us reluctant to upgrade certain buildings due to liking the way the area feels with its existing building stock - something where functionality may be more important for some players, and aesthetics for others.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 65 - Materials for Tiers
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/a58850f831ee951fc4386718ec2d4f1b4275ae68.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
John here this week, I want to talk to you a little about how the decisions and balancing choices we have been making recently are going to affect our art assets.

We have previously told you about our decisions towards tiers of development in the game and how players will progress through them. We are currently working with a wood tier, stone tier and a metal tier. 
In terms of what those tiers can look like, and how they can shape the world as you grow through it; I am working on defining materials which can be used with each tier. We currently made our buildings (which are the clearest representation of the tiers) based on how we wanted them to look. We have been influenced by some of our favourite games and the styles of typical buildings for specific functions and also limited by time and skill. I needed to produce a certain amount of buildings for early access release and now that we have had longer to consider what the game should ultimately look like, I have been making some rules for creating the new buildings - or replacing the placeholder (barracks anyone?) buildings that we put into the game when we didn’t have a clear idea of how we wanted something to look.

When you first land on the island and you do not have access to most materials, we are thinking that basic thatch and simple timber construction should be where you start. This is reflected in the cover image today with the new representation of the swordsman watchpost. The structure is made of bamboo poles which are easy to cut down and manipulate, tied together and a thatch roof to shelter from the elements.

As you progress through the game and upgrade your sawmill, you will unlock the ability for creating beams and planks out of hardwoods to develop your building stock further. 

Similarly, when you start with stone gathering, you will unlock cobblestone construction and the upgrades will lead to hewn stone blocks for more advanced building types. 

We think the developing buildings and representations of level through their material types will lead to a rich variety throughout your villages. We have said before about how charming your bases feel when you start fleshing them out and how we want to include variations when you place a building. Rows of the same building will still feel individual while creating a streetscape. Having different buildings at different stages of the tiers will add to this and enhance that variety.

We look forward to seeing the developments you all craft!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 64 - Gravesites and Bird's Nests
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/6335e7dcd0824d43cfffb467e4115768572a753c.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week, I had said that I would show one or two new biomes today, but I realised halfway through the week that it would be more efficient to first finish the mountains for all biomes and then populate them than going biome by biome. So, instead I will give you a quick update on some of the additional considerations we’ve given to loot and exploring.

Two weeks ago, I talked about exploration, rewards, and accessibility of areas. Based on what we said in that post, we have been trying to give each path a reward, and we have been thinking further about what these rewards should look like (and be).

To start with, we found that even when you find something, you can currently only find chests. Chests were always meant to just be placeholders, but we did not expect for the simple visual monotony to be affecting the fun of the exploration so much. So we want to introduce more ‘things’ to find. 

Now “things” come in three varieties: Content, visual, and mechanic.

Addressing content first, we want the type of thing the player finds to have an actual impact on the way they play the game. While that can't be the case for every single exploration reward (there will continue to be simple coin or food or ammo rewards), there will have to be more substantial rewards, such as types of seeds or rare goods which make players wonder if their current find doesn’t substantially reduce the cost or increase the benefit of a certain way to play. Ideally, we want this to result in players changing their tactics as they progress, so the games feel more varied to them rather than starting with a set plan in mind and not deviating from that. They can of course choose to do so - but it may prove inferior to responding to what the map provides for you.

As we will talk about soon, 0.9 will introduce a research tree to unlock buildings, productivity bonuses, and even items for the commander. We think this will provide us with a good amount of options for exploration rewards as we intend them, and should be what the players are “looking for” when they go exploring. As an example, a player may find an upgrade to the productivity of their miners - even though they had chosen to go with farming for money, this may incentivise them to switch to the now more lucrative mining.

The second part to address is visuals. We have found that finding the same two types of chests (poor or rich) over and over, with random rewards in them, just does not have the desired effect of being excited about what you have found. Considering the chest “could” contain something cool - or simply some wheat - we almost automatically keep our own excitement in check, which isn’t a great outcome. 

As you can see from today’s image, we are starting to experiment with some options other than chests. The gravesite in the image was one quick idea on an alternative for what you might find (we also thought of buried treasure, bird’s nests, special plants, etc) - which could help create a narrower range of expectations. If you find a bird’s nest, you may find some feathers or similar natural materials in them - if you find a buried treasure, you can expect gold coins, bars, maybe some gems. Overall, you will then know what value of loot to expect from what you can see, which should mean that you can get back to getting super excited about some of the rewards once you see them.

Finally, we have also been considering different “mechanics” for loot, other than just “point and get something”. For example, we thought of “neutral” animals that may be walking around, which you can attack (and then have to fight) if you want a payoff - or you can choose to ignore for the time being if you are low on health, or don’t want to handle the situation quite yet. The gravesite was also chosen as today’s image for that reason - rifling through a grave should come with some moral dilemma, so we will have to consider some negative effects that may happen if you choose to dig through them, but you may choose to do so for the reward. For example, a disease may offset your advantage from epic loot by debuffing the villagers you come into contact with.

While we intend to have some of the visual and loot changes ready for 0.8, we are not expecting for the mechanic changes to happen until 0.10, so hang in there! That doesn’t stop us from being able to mix up the nodes for now though, so we gain variety.

Until next week!
